newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of China '96 deposits up 12.5 pct - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China '96 deposits up 12.5 pct - paper.

text.p: The Bank of China group posted a 12.5 percent growth in deposits to HK$629.4 billion in 1996, representing about a quarter of Hong Kong's total deposit at the end of 1996, newspapers said on Friday.
Lending grew 14 percent to HK$350.9 billion in 1996, while doubtful debts accounted for 0.7 percent of the total lending and bad debts made up of 1.3 percent, they said.
The group's mortgage business rose nine percent and the loan-to-deposit ratio was 55.75 percent, the papers reported.
Its assets expanded 6.4 percent to HK$980 billion.
The banking group expected to increase the portion of Hong Kong banknotes it issued by four to five percent a year for the next two years, the newspapers said.
The Bank of China group currently issues about 11 percent of Hong Kong dollar banknotes in circulation.

Lam Kwong-siu, the group's deputy chief executive, was quoted by the newspaper as saying the interest margin was likely to continue to narrow in 1997. The bank's interest margin was about 2.7 percent.
The Bank of China group reported a 20.5 percent growth in pre-tax profit in 1996, they said.
